# AGENTS.md — GitHub Actions

Linux pull-request jobs in `ci.yml` feed the required `all checks passed` verdict; Wine runs Windows Node on hosted Linux only in `ci-master.yml`. Master-only platform checks, Linux/Windows self-hosted standbys, and manual runner benchmarks live in `ci-master.yml`, which listens to master pushes and `workflow_dispatch`, not `pull_request`; separating workflow triggers keeps master-only jobs out of PR check panels. The master standbys validate the self-hosted failover targets; preserve the existing per-platform switches (values `selfhosted` for the in-house standbys and `blacksmith` for Blacksmith's hosted runners) and the Dependabot hosted fallback under the `selfhosted` values ([failover runbook](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-ci-failover-runbook.md), [blacksmith failover leg note](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-09-09-blacksmith-failover-leg.md)).

The merge checks run from three workflows named `Policy`, which run on `pull_request_target` so their definitions come from master, and call the `deepseek-harness-check` action directly: `pr-check-on-head-branch.yml` on pull-request updates gives `Policy / Master Change` and `Policy / Pre-Merge Check`, `pr-check-after-approve.yml` on pull-request updates and submitted or dismissed reviews gives `Policy / Approve Check`, which also publishes the review verdict as the check run `Policy / Reviewer Check`, and `pr-check-on-base-branch.yml` on master pushes re-runs the head-branch checks as `Policy / Recheck`. Branch rules require those check names, so keep the job names and the workflow name. Each job reads its mode from a repository variable: `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF`, `MERGE_POLICY_PRE_MERGE`, and `MERGE_POLICY_HEAD_DIFF`, each `off` (skip), `report` (run without failing the job), or `block` (fail the job); a missing value or an unknown one counts as `report`. `MERGE_POLICY_HEAD_DIFF` decides whether `Policy / Approve Check` runs and fails; while it runs, `Policy / Reviewer Check` is published whatever that mode says, with `success` when every file that needs review has one and `action_required` with the reviewers to ask otherwise. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` merges the commit `Policy / Master Change` reports, so it runs only after that job and stays off while `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF` is `off`; a merge it cannot do and a build that fails both follow its own mode, so `report` warns and skips the build while `block` fails the job. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` runs `scripts/pre-merge-check.ts` under plain Node and knows nothing else about the merged tree: that script checks the released manifests against the root version, installs, and builds the Host and Client contracts, so change it in one pull request together with the build it orchestrates.
